hypertension.explanation: Your blood pressure is higher than normal, which means your heart is working harder to pump blood through your body.

diabetes.explanation: Your body has difficulty controlling the amount of sugar in your blood, either because it doesn't produce enough insulin or can't use it properly.

myocardial_infarction.explanation: A blocked artery has prevented blood flow to part of your heart muscle, causing damage.

pneumonia.explanation: An infection in your lungs has caused inflammation and filled air sacs with fluid, making it hard to breathe.

arrhythmia.explanation: Your heart is beating too fast, too slow, or in an irregular pattern.

hyperlipidemia.explanation: You have too much cholesterol (a fatty substance) in your blood, which can build up in your arteries.

anemia.explanation: You don't have enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen throughout your body.

hypothyroidism.explanation: Your thyroid gland isn't producing enough hormones, which slows down your metabolism.

gastritis.explanation: The lining of your stomach is inflamed or irritated.

arthritis.explanation: One or more of your joints are inflamed, causing pain, stiffness, and reduced movement.

asthma.explanation: Your airways are inflamed and narrowed, making it hard to breathe, especially during physical activity.

COPD.explanation: Long-term damage to your lungs makes it progressively harder to breathe.

stroke.explanation: A blood vessel in your brain was blocked or burst, preventing blood flow to brain tissue.

CKD.explanation: Your kidneys aren't filtering waste from your blood properly, and this happens gradually over time.

normal.explanation: This test result is healthy and in the expected range for you.

abnormal.explanation: This test result is higher or lower than the expected range, which may need attention.

critical.explanation: This result is severely outside the normal range and requires immediate medical attention.

pending.explanation: This test result is not yet available; the lab is still analyzing the sample.

fasting.explanation: You should not have any food or beverages (except water) before this test to ensure accurate results.

medication_hold.explanation: Don't take your usual medications before this test; your doctor will tell you when to resume them.

bed_rest.explanation: You should remain in bed and avoid physical activity to allow your body to recover.

follow_up.explanation: You need to schedule another visit with your doctor to review results or check your progress.

as_needed.explanation: You can take this medication whenever you feel you need it, but follow the dosage instructions.

mild.explanation: Your condition is minor and should improve with basic treatment or time.

moderate.explanation: Your condition needs medical attention and treatment to prevent it from getting worse.

severe.explanation: Your condition is serious and requires immediate medical intervention.
